title: Family grieving the loss of 'tiny, frail' woman known as Mama D
subtitle: The chronic lung condition meant her mother had a hoarse voice had to raise her voice to be heard, which may have been misconstrued as yelling or being belligerent, Noname said.
article: Samantha Noname wants people to know her mother, Deanna Noname, was a good woman.
Deanna Noname, 55, died in police custody on Aug. 7 after being arrested the day before and family members are waiting for the truth about how she died.
"My mom was a good woman, she was well loved, well known," Noname said, speaking on the phone from Calgary. "Everybody knew her as Mama D."

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team is currently investigating the death. According to ASIRT, the Edmonton Police Service responded to the Belvedere LRT station where they took the 55-year-old woman and two others into custody.

The woman, who ASIRT has not named, was first taken to the northeast division police office and later to the detainee management unit at police headquarters. She was charged with causing a disturbance, breach of recognizance and was being held on additional warrants for theft and failure to appear.
During a cell check on Aug. 7 around 10 a.m., she was found on the floor in medical distress, unresponsive with laboured breathing.

Her mother was tiny and frail and had been diagnosed previously with COPD. The chronic lung condition meant her mother had a hoarse voice and had to raise her voice to be heard, which may have been misconstrued as yelling or being belligerent, Noname said.
Since her mother died, Noname has been smudging and praying and trying to comfort her family.
"I'm still sad my mom's gone," Noname said.
Noname said her mother had quit drinking, contrary to reports that her mother was intoxicated.
Her mother had her inhalers in her purse, which was seized by police while she was in custody, Noname said.
The 55-year-old woman would go out on walks in hopes of building lung capacity, as recommended by her doctor.
At the time, she did not have her oxygen tank with her and had asked for it while being held in custody, Noname said.
She added she has known others who have been denied medical treatment while in custody.
Noname disputes the ASIRT report that there were no significant injuries, stating her mother had bruising on her body and a bump on her head.
She said she hopes justice will be served.
"I miss her already, I miss her everyday," Noname said.
